proof: AD∥BC, so △ABC and △DBC have common base BC and equal altitudes; hence [ABC]=[DBC].
The diagonals meet at interior point O, so [ABC]=[OAB]+[OBC] and [DBC]=[ODC]+[OBC]. Subtracting the common [OBC] yields [OAB]=[ODC].
For (2), △OAB and △OBC have bases AO and OC on line AC and share the altitude from B; therefore [OAB]:[OBC]=AO:OC=3:5. Since [ODC]=12 and [OAB]=[ODC], [OBC]=12×5/3=20 cm².
